Ministry (EN): Education, Sport, Youth, Research and Innovation
Question (EN): Could the Minister state how many primary and secondary school students participated in the Digital Literacy Programme during the academic year 2023/2024, broken down by region?
Answer (EN): A total of 27,450 primary school students and 22,890 secondary school students participated in the Digital Literacy Programme during the academic year 2023/2024. Participation was highest in the Northern and Southern regions.

Question (EN): How many long-term care beds are currently available in public and private long-term care facilities across Malta, and how many of these are occupied as of the latest data?
Answer (EN): As of 20/03/2024, there are 3,150 long-term care beds available in public facilities, with 2,980 occupied, and 1,890 beds in private facilities, with 1,760 occupied.

Question (EN): What is the expected completion timeline for the ongoing roadworks along Triq iż-Żgħażagħ in Qormi and Triq il-Kbira in Rabat?
Answer (EN): The roadworks along Triq iż-Żgħażagħ in Qormi are expected to be completed by 30/06/2024, while the works along Triq il-Kbira in Rabat are projected to finish by 15/08/2024.

Ministry (EN): Environment, Energy and Regeneration of the Grand Harbour
Question (EN): How many active restoration projects for green spaces are currently underway by the Ministry, and what is the total acreage covered by these projects?
Answer (EN): There are 12 active restoration projects for green spaces, covering a total acreage of 45.7 hectares.

Question (EN): Please provide the payment schedule for the Child Benefit for the year 2024, including the specific dates for each quarterly payment.
Answer (EN): The Child Benefit payment schedule for 2024 is as follows: Q1 - 15/04/2024, Q2 - 15/07/2024, Q3 - 15/10/2024, and Q4 - 15/01/2025.

Ministry (EN): Home Affairs, Security, Reforms and Equality
Question (EN): Which police stations in Malta have been earmarked for structural upgrades in 2024, and what is the allocated budget for each station?
Answer (EN): The police stations earmarked for upgrades in 2024 are St. Julian’s, Sliema, Mosta, and Gozo, with allocated budgets of €2.1 million, €1.8 million, €1.5 million, and €1.2 million respectively.

Question (EN): How many applications for SME grants were submitted in 2023, and what percentage of these were approved?
Answer (EN): A total of 1,240 applications for SME grants were submitted in 2023, of which 89% (1,104 applications) were approved.

Question (EN): What is the current average processing time for the issuance of national identity cards in Malta as of April 2024?
Answer (EN): As of April 2024, the average processing time for the issuance of national identity cards is 12 working days.

Ministry (EN): Justice and Reform of the Construction Sector
Question (EN): What is the average duration from application to approval for building permits in Gozo as compared to Malta over the past two years?
Answer (EN): In Gozo, the average duration for building permit approval is 84 days, while in Malta, it is 72 days over the past two years.

Question (EN): What is the current frequency of public transport services in Gozo during peak and off-peak hours?
Answer (EN): During peak hours, public transport services in Gozo operate every 15-20 minutes, while during off-peak hours, the frequency is every 30-45 minutes.

Ministry (EN): Justice and Reform of the Construction Sector
Title (EN): Delays in Processing Construction Permits - Lack of Transparency
Question (EN): To ask the Minister responsible for Justice and Reform of the Construction Sector what measures are being taken to address the alarming backlog in construction permit applications, with reports indicating processing times exceeding 18 months, and whether there is a lack of transparency in prioritisation criteria?
Answer (EN): The Ministry acknowledges the importance of timely processing of construction permits and is implementing measures to streamline procedures. A dedicated task force has been established to assess and expedite applications. Prioritisation is based on statutory deadlines and critical project timelines, with full transparency maintained through quarterly updates on the Ministry's official website.

Title (EN): Hospital Equipment Procurement - Failure to Meet Urgent Needs
Question (EN): To ask the Minister responsible for Health and Active Ageing why procurement for essential medical equipment, such as MRI machines and surgical tools, continues to be delayed, despite repeated assurances of urgency, and whether this reflects a systemic failure in public health procurement?
Answer (EN): The Ministry is actively pursuing procurement for critical medical equipment. Bidding processes have been initiated, and the necessary funds have been allocated. Delays are primarily due to stringent EU tendering regulations, which must be adhered to for compliance. The Ministry remains committed to ensuring these lifesaving resources are delivered as swiftly as possible.

Title (EN): Public Transport Reliability - Chronic Service Disruptions
Question (EN): To ask the Minister responsible for Transport, Infrastructure and Public Works what concrete actions are being taken to address the persistent unreliability of public transport services, with commuters reporting an average of three breakdowns per week per bus line, and whether this indicates a failure in infrastructure maintenance?
Answer (EN): The Ministry recognises the frustration caused by service disruptions and has allocated additional funds for emergency repairs and preventive maintenance. A real-time monitoring system is being implemented to identify and address issues promptly. The reliability of public transport remains a priority, and the Ministry is committed to delivering consistent service.

Ministry (EN): Environment, Energy and Regeneration of the Grand Harbour
Title (EN): Grand Harbour Regeneration - Missing Deadlines and Unfulfilled Promises
Question (EN): To ask the Minister responsible for Environment, Energy and Regeneration of the Grand Harbour why the regeneration projects for the Grand Harbour are falling behind schedule, with key milestones such as the new cruise liner terminal and waterfront promenade delayed by over two years, and whether this reflects mismanagement of EU funds?
Answer (EN): The Ministry is aware of the delays in Grand Harbour regeneration projects and is actively working to accelerate progress. Challenges such as unforeseen archaeological findings and procurement delays have impacted timelines. The Ministry assures that all projects are on track to meet revised deadlines, with EU funds being utilised in full compliance with regulations.

Title (EN): Child Protection Services - Inadequate Support for Vulnerable Families
Question (EN): To ask the Minister responsible for Social Policy and Children's Rights what steps are being taken to address the critical shortage of social workers and caseworkers in child protection services, which has left hundreds of vulnerable families without adequate support, and whether this constitutes a breach of the state's duty of care?
Answer (EN): The Ministry is actively recruiting additional social workers and caseworkers to address staffing shortages. Training programmes have been expanded, and temporary measures such as outsourcing have been implemented to fill gaps. The Ministry remains fully committed to safeguarding the welfare of children and vulnerable families.

Ministry (EN): Education, Sport, Youth, Research and Innovation
Title (EN): School Infrastructure Failures - Persistent Structural Issues
Question (EN): To ask the Minister responsible for Education, Sport, Youth, Research and Innovation why so many state schools continue to suffer from structural failures such as leaking roofs, cracked walls, and inadequate ventilation, despite repeated pledges to address these issues, and whether this reflects a failure in long-term planning?
Answer (EN): The Ministry has identified the most critical infrastructure issues and is prioritising repairs through a phased approach. A comprehensive audit of all state schools has been conducted, and necessary funds have been allocated. The Ministry assures that all structural issues will be resolved within the next two years.

Ministry (EN): Home Affairs, Security, Reforms and Equality
Title (EN): Police Response Times - Failure to Meet National Standards
Question (EN): To ask the Minister responsible for Home Affairs, Security, Reforms and Equality why police response times in high-density areas continue to exceed national benchmarks, with emergency calls taking an average of 20 minutes to be addressed, and whether this indicates a systemic failure in resource allocation?
Answer (EN): The Ministry is reviewing police deployment strategies to improve response times in high-density areas. Additional resources, including patrol vehicles and personnel, have been allocated. A new digital dispatch system is being implemented to enhance coordination and efficiency.

Title (EN): Land Registry Delays - Impact on Economic Growth
Question (EN): To ask the Minister responsible for Economy, European Funds and Lands what measures are being taken to address the chronic delays in the Land Registry, which are stifling economic growth by preventing timely property transactions and business expansions, and whether this reflects inefficiencies in digital transformation?
Answer (EN): The Ministry is accelerating the digitalisation of the Land Registry to reduce processing times. A new online platform is being developed to streamline transactions, and additional staff have been recruited. The Ministry assures that these measures will significantly reduce delays within the next 12 months.

Title (EN): Government Accountability - Failure to Deliver on Key Promises
Question (EN): To ask the Prime Minister why several key government promises, including the introduction of a national minimum wage and the expansion of free childcare services, remain unfulfilled two years after taking office, and whether this reflects a lack of political will or administrative incompetence?
Answer (EN): The government remains committed to delivering on its promises, including the introduction of a national minimum wage and expanded childcare services. These initiatives require careful planning and consultation with stakeholders to ensure successful implementation. Progress updates will be provided in due course.

Title (EN): Gozo Ferry Service Failures - Chronic Delays and Cancellations
Question (EN): To ask the Minister responsible for Gozo why the Gozo ferry service continues to experience chronic delays and cancellations, with passengers stranded for hours and businesses in Gozo suffering financial losses, and whether this constitutes a breach of the state's duty to ensure reliable connectivity?
Answer (EN): The Ministry is addressing operational challenges in the Gozo ferry service through increased maintenance and additional vessel deployments. A new scheduling system is being tested to improve reliability. The Ministry assures that these measures will significantly enhance service consistency in the coming months.

Question (EN): In view of the upcoming disbursement of EU Recovery and Resilience Facility funds, can the Prime Minister provide a detailed breakdown of how the allocated €150 million will be distributed across sectors, including the projected timeline for each disbursement tranche?
Answer (EN): The Government confirms that a comprehensive allocation plan for the €150 million in EU Recovery and Resilience Facility funds has been finalised and will be tabled in Parliament within the next two weeks. The plan outlines sectoral distributions, including €60 million for healthcare infrastructure, €45 million for green energy initiatives, and €30 million for digital transformation in public administration, with disbursements scheduled quarterly starting from Q3 2024.

Ministry (EN): Justice and Reform of the Construction Sector
Question (EN): Given persistent complaints regarding delays in processing construction permits, can the Minister for Justice and Reform of the Construction Sector provide a written list of all applications pending approval for over six months, including the reasons for such delays and a concrete action plan to resolve them within the next three months?
Answer (EN): The Ministry acknowledges delays in permit processing and has identified 187 applications pending for over six months due to incomplete documentation or technical review requirements. A dedicated task force has been established to resolve these cases within 90 days, with weekly progress reports to be shared with stakeholders. The Minister will table a full list of delayed cases by 15/04/2024.

Ministry (EN): Environment, Energy and Regeneration of the Grand Harbour
Question (EN): Can the Minister confirm whether the contract for the Grand Harbour regeneration project has been awarded, and if so, provide the name of the selected contractor, the total contract value, and the expected completion timeline?
Answer (EN): The contract for the Grand Harbour regeneration project was awarded to Mediterranean Infrastructure Partners Ltd. on 28/03/2024, with a total value of €85 million. The project is scheduled for completion in phases, with the first phase (harbourfront promenade) due by December 2026 and the second phase (maritime museum and cultural centre) by December 2027.

Ministry (EN): Education, Sport, Youth, Research and Innovation
Question (EN): Given the recent announcement of a new national digital learning platform, can the Minister for Education provide all tender documents, evaluation criteria, and the names of the shortlisted bidders for this project?
Answer (EN): The Ministry confirms that the tender for the national digital learning platform was issued on 01/03/2024, with three shortlisted bidders: EdTech Malta Ltd., LearnFlow Solutions, and Global Education Systems. The full tender dossier, including evaluation criteria, has been published on the Ministry’s website and is available for public scrutiny. The final selection is expected by 30/06/2024.

Ministry (EN): Home Affairs, Security, Reforms and Equality
Question (EN): Can the Minister for Home Affairs provide a detailed implementation roadmap for the ongoing police reform, including key milestones, responsible entities, and a projected timeline for full operationalisation of the new Police Service Act?
Answer (EN): The Government confirms that the police reform implementation roadmap has been finalised and will be published by 30/04/2024. Key milestones include the establishment of the Independent Police Complaints Board by Q3 2024, the rollout of community policing units by Q1 2025, and full operationalisation of the Police Service Act by Q4 2025. Regular progress updates will be tabled in Parliament.

Question (EN): Can the Minister for Social Policy provide a breakdown of all government funding allocated to childcare services in the past three years, including the number of children benefiting from subsidised childcare and the average subsidy per child?
Answer (EN): The Ministry confirms that annual funding for childcare services has increased from €12 million in 2021 to €18 million in 2024. Over the past three years, an average of 4,200 children per year have benefited from subsidised childcare, with the average subsidy rising from €250 to €350 per month. A detailed breakdown by year and locality will be tabled by 10/05/2024.

Question (EN): Can the Minister for Health provide a full list of all medical equipment procured for Mater Dei Hospital in the past 12 months, including the suppliers, contract values, and expected delivery dates?
Answer (EN): The Ministry confirms that 12 major equipment procurement contracts were finalised for Mater Dei Hospital in the past year, valued at a total of €15 million. A full list, including suppliers such as MedTech Solutions Ltd. and BioMedical Equipment Malta, contract values ranging from €500,000 to €2.3 million, and delivery schedules from Q2 2024 to Q1 2025, will be tabled by 15/05/2024.

Question (EN): Given reports of delays in land valuation appeals, can the Minister for Economy provide a written list of all pending land valuation appeals, including the date of submission, estimated resolution timeline, and the reasons for any delays?
Answer (EN): The Ministry acknowledges 47 pending land valuation appeals, with an average processing time of 12 months. The main causes of delay are incomplete documentation in 22 cases and complex legal disputes in 15 cases. A task force has been set up to resolve 30 cases by Q4 2024, with the full list to be published on the Ministry’s website by 20/05/2024.

Question (EN): Can the Minister for Transport confirm whether the contractor for the public transport enhancements project has met the agreed milestones, and if not, provide a revised timeline for completion along with reasons for any delays?
Answer (EN): The Ministry confirms that the contractor, Malta Transport Solutions, has met all agreed milestones for the public transport enhancements project, including the installation of new bus shelters and digital signage. The project is on track for completion by December 2024, with 85% of works already finalised. A full progress report will be published by 31/05/2024.

Question (EN): Can the Minister for Gozo provide all documentation related to the evaluation of tenders for the new Gozo Channel service, including the names of the shortlisted bidders, the evaluation criteria applied, and the projected timeline for the award of the contract?
Answer (EN): The Ministry confirms that the tender evaluation for the new Gozo Channel service is underway, with three shortlisted bidders: Gozo Maritime Services, Malta Ferry Operations, and Grand Harbour Ferries. The evaluation criteria include vessel capacity, frequency, and sustainability, with the final selection expected by 30/06/2024. All tender documents and evaluation frameworks will be published on the Ministry’s website by 31/05/2024.

Question (EN): Parking Spaces - Dedicated Spaces for Disabled Persons in Valletta
Answer (EN): As of the latest quarterly report, Valletta has a total of 412 dedicated parking spaces for disabled persons, with 28 additional spaces reserved for electric vehicles. These figures reflect an increase of 15% compared to 2022, following infrastructural upgrades completed in Q4 2023. All new construction projects in Valletta are now legally required to include disabled parking in their plans.

Question (EN): Construction Permits - Average Processing Time in 2023
Answer (EN): In 2023, the average processing time for construction permits across Malta was 47 calendar days, a reduction of 8 days from the previous year. This improvement was achieved through the implementation of digital workflows and increased staffing in the Planning Authority. The shortest processing times were recorded for minor residential alterations (21 days), while major commercial projects averaged 89 days.

Question (EN): Energy Efficiency - Number of Retrofitted Public Buildings in 2023
Answer (EN): A total of 127 public buildings underwent energy efficiency retrofits in 2023, surpassing the annual target of 100 by 27%. These retrofits included installation of LED lighting, solar panels, and smart heating systems. The most significant projects were completed in state schools and health centres. The total investment amounted to €18.5 million.

Question (EN): Social Housing - Number of Completed Units in 2023
Answer (EN): In 2023, 432 social housing units were completed across Malta, including 158 in Gozo. These units comprise a mix of affordable rental properties and shared ownership schemes. The completion rate exceeded the annual target by 8%, with 12 new projects initiated in the final quarter of 2023.

Question (EN): School Infrastructure - Number of Schools Requiring Urgent Repairs
Answer (EN): As of February 2024, 23 state schools across Malta have been identified as requiring urgent structural repairs. These schools have been prioritised in the 2024-2025 capital works programme, with €12 million allocated for remedial works. The ministry is also exploring public-private partnerships to accelerate the rehabilitation of school buildings.

Question (EN): Healthcare Staffing - Number of Nurses Recruited in 2023
Answer (EN): In 2023, a total of 342 nurses were recruited into the public healthcare system, the highest annual intake in the past decade. This includes 89 newly graduated nurses from the University of Malta. Additionally, 112 foreign nurses were recruited to address critical shortages in specialised departments.

Question (EN): Transport Infrastructure - Completion Date for Marsa Flyover
Answer (EN): The Marsa Flyover is scheduled for completion by 30th September 2024, with 92% of the structural work already finalised. The project is on track to deliver a traffic flow improvement of 40% in the Marsa locality, as per the revised traffic impact assessment.

Question (EN): Grand Harbour Regeneration - Total Investment to Date
Answer (EN): To date, a total of €268 million has been invested in the Grand Harbour regeneration project since its inception in 2020. This includes €89 million allocated in the 2024 national budget. The project has created 312 direct employment opportunities and 547 indirect jobs, primarily in the maritime and construction sectors.

Question (EN): Youth Employment - Number of Internships Offered in 2023
Answer (EN): In 2023, the Government facilitated 2,145 internships for Maltese youth under the 'Youth Guarantee' programme. Of these, 1,287 were in private sector companies, while 858 were in public entities. The average stipend provided was €850 per month, with €420,000 allocated from the European Social Fund.

Question (EN): Gozo - Number of New Residential Units Completed in 2023
Answer (EN): In 2023, 189 new residential units were completed in Gozo. This includes 94 affordable housing units under the 'Housing Gozo' initiative and 45 units financed through private investment. The remaining 50 units were self-build schemes approved by the Gozo Ministry. The completion rate represents a 14% increase over 2022.

Question (EN): Public Transport Routes - Review Progress
Answer (EN): The Ministry for Transport, Infrastructure and Public Works is currently reviewing public transport routes as part of its ongoing strategic planning. A comprehensive report highlighting key updates and proposed changes will be shared with stakeholders in due course.

Question (EN): Grand Harbour Regeneration - Budget Allocation
Answer (EN): The Ministry for the Environment, Energy and Regeneration of the Grand Harbour is actively reviewing budgetary allocations for regeneration projects. Further details on allocations will be finalised following consultations with relevant stakeholders.

Question (EN): School Infrastructure - Maintenance Backlog
Answer (EN): The Ministry for Education, Sport, Youth, Research and Innovation is addressing maintenance backlogs in school infrastructure through a phased approach. Progress reports are regularly updated and shared with the relevant authorities.

Question (EN): Construction Sector Reform - Licensing Delays
Answer (EN): The Ministry for Justice and Reform of the Construction Sector is streamlining licensing processes to reduce delays. Enhanced digital tools are being implemented to improve efficiency, with further updates expected in the coming months.

Question (EN): Health Services - Emergency Department Wait Times
Answer (EN): The Ministry for Health and Active Ageing is continuously monitoring emergency department wait times. Measures to improve patient flow are being evaluated, with results anticipated within the next quarter.

Question (EN): Gozo - Direct Air Connectivity Enhancements
Answer (EN): The Ministry for Gozo is exploring options to enhance direct air connectivity between Gozo and mainland Malta. Discussions with aviation stakeholders are underway to assess feasibility and potential timelines.

Question (EN): Social Housing - Allocation Criteria Update
Answer (EN): The Ministry for Social Policy and Children's Rights is reviewing social housing allocation criteria to ensure fairness and transparency. A revised framework is expected to be introduced following public consultation.

Question (EN): Energy Efficiency - National Incentives Programme
Answer (EN): The Ministry for the Environment, Energy and Regeneration of the Grand Harbour is evaluating national incentives to promote energy efficiency. A detailed proposal will be presented to Cabinet for approval in the near future.

Question (EN): Youth Employment - Skills Development Initiatives
Answer (EN): The Ministry for Education, Sport, Youth, Research and Innovation is actively developing skills enhancement programmes for youth employment. Pilot initiatives are being tested, with broader rollout planned subject to evaluation.

Question (EN): Public Sector Reform - Digital Transformation
Answer (EN): The Ministry for the Prime Minister is advancing digital transformation initiatives across the public sector. Progress updates are regularly shared with the relevant parliamentary committees as part of ongoing transparency efforts.

Answer (EN): The topic falls under the ambit of the Ministry for Home Affairs, Security, Reforms and Equality. The Honourable Member will receive a comprehensive response at the next appropriate parliamentary session.

Answer (EN): The matter raised is pertinent to the Ministry for Health and Active Ageing. The Honourable Member is directed to await the formal response to be delivered during the sitting on 29/10/2024.
